# Toast Notification Queue Manager (Capacitor Toast, Web)

## Background

The `@capacitor/toast` plugin exposes a single fire-and-forget `Toast.show(...)` method. On the **web** implementation, calling `Toast.show(...)` immediately appends a `<pwa-toast>` element to `document.body` and resolves right away — it does **not** wait for the toast to finish, does **not** remove the element, and gives no way to prevent multiple toasts from piling up on top of each other.

Your job is to build a **toast queue manager** on top of the Capacitor Toast web plugin that serializes many `show` calls so that toasts are displayed strictly one after another (never overlapping), with configurable per-toast display duration and screen position, plus an API to enqueue toasts and to await the queue draining completely. The manager must behave deterministically even when a large burst of `enqueue` calls arrives synchronously.

## Requirements

* Build a small web app that imports the real `@capacitor/toast` plugin and uses its **web implementation** (no native platform is available).
* Implement a queue manager that:
  * Displays queued toasts strictly sequentially in FIFO (enqueue) order — never more than one toast element present at the same time.
  * Uses the real `Toast.show(...)` API to create each toast (so a `<pwa-toast>` element is appended to `document.body` for every displayed toast).
  * Supports a configurable display duration and position per toast.
  * Removes each displayed `<pwa-toast>` element once its duration has elapsed, before starting the next toast.
  * Handles rapid synchronous bursts of enqueue calls deterministically and in order.
* Expose the queue API on the global `window` object so it can be driven from the browser console / an automation script.

## Implementation Hints

* Use a bundler (Vite is recommended) so the `@capacitor/toast` npm module can be imported and run in a plain browser. On web, `Toast.show(...)` resolves immediately after appending `<pwa-toast>`, so the manager itself owns the display timing and the element cleanup.
* Because `Toast.show(...)` resolves before the toast is actually done, chain the queue with promises/timers so the next toast starts only after the current one's duration has fully elapsed and its element has been removed.
* The Capacitor Toast `ShowOptions.duration` only accepts `'short'` (2000ms) or `'long'` (3500ms); your manager's own numeric duration controls the real sequencing/cleanup timing, independent of that coarse plugin value.
* Project path: `/home/user/toast-queue`
* Build command: `npm run build`
* Start command: `npm run preview` (must serve the built app at `http://localhost:4173`)
* Port: `4173`
* The served page MUST attach the following API to `window`:
  * `window.enqueueToast(options)` — `options` is an object `{ text: string, duration?: number | 'short' | 'long', position?: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom' }`. `duration` as a number is the display time in **milliseconds**; the string `'short'` maps to `2000` and `'long'` maps to `3500`; when omitted it defaults to `2000`. `position` defaults to `'bottom'`. It returns a `Promise<void>` that resolves ONLY after this specific toast has been displayed for its full duration AND its `<pwa-toast>` element has been removed.
  * `window.drainToastQueue()` — returns a `Promise<void>` that resolves when the queue is empty and no toast is currently active; if called while already idle it resolves immediately.
  * `window.getQueueState()` — returns synchronously an object `{ pending: number, active: boolean }`, where `pending` is the number of toasts waiting (not yet shown) and `active` is whether a toast is currently being displayed.
* Observable display contract (these are the outcomes checked in a headless browser):
  * Every displayed toast is created via the real `Toast.show(...)`, so it appears as a `<pwa-toast>` element in `document.body`. Each such element MUST carry the toast text on its `text` property (as set by the plugin) and MUST have a `data-position` attribute equal to that toast's resolved position.
  * At no point may more than one `<pwa-toast>` element exist in the document at the same time.
  * `<pwa-toast>` elements must appear in the exact order the toasts were enqueued.
  * Each `<pwa-toast>` element must remain in the document for approximately its configured duration and then be removed before the next one appears.

3. **ToastQueueManager class**:

   - Has an internal flag/slot indicating if a toast is currently active
   - `enqueue(options)` — adds to queue, returns promise that resolves when this toast finishes

```typescript
import { Toast } from '@capacitor/toast';

interface ToastOptions {
  text: string;
  duration?: number | 'short' | 'long';
  position?: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom';
}

interface QueueEntry {
  options: ToastOptions;
  text: string;
  durationMs: number;
  position: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom';
  resolve: () => void;
  reject: (err: unknown) => void;
}

class ToastQueueManager {
  private queue: QueueEntry[] = [];
  private active: boolean = false;
  private idleResolvers: Array<() => void> = [];

  enqueue(options: ToastOptions): Promise<void> {
    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const text = options.text;
      const position = options.position ?? 'bottom';
      let durationMs: number;
      if (typeof options.duration === 'number') {
        durationMs = options.duration;
      } else if (options.duration === 'long') {
        durationMs = 3500;
      } else {
        // 'short' or undefined
        durationMs = 2000;
      }
      const entry: QueueEntry = { options, text, durationMs, position, resolve, reject };
      this.queue.push(entry);
      this.scheduleNext();
    });
  }

  drain(): Promise<void> {
    return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
      if (this.queue.length === 0 && !this.active) {
        resolve();
      } else {
        this.idleResolvers.push(resolve);
      }
    });
  }

  getState(): { pending: number; active: boolean } {
    return { pending: this.queue.length, active: this.active };
  }

  private scheduleNext(): void {
    if (this.active) return;
    if (this.queue.length === 0) {
      // Queue empty and no active, flush idle resolvers
      const resolvers = this.idleResolvers;
      this.idleResolvers = [];
      for (const r of resolvers) r();
      return;
    }
    const entry = this.queue.shift()!;
    this.active = true;
    this.displayToast(entry).finally(() => {
      this.active = false;
      // notify drain resolvers if queue is empty
      if (this.queue.length === 0) {
        const resolvers = this.idleResolvers;
        this.idleResolvers = [];
        for (const r of resolvers) r();
      } else {
        this.scheduleNext();
      }
    });
  }

  private async displayToast(entry: QueueEntry): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await Toast.show({
        text: entry.text,
        duration: entry.durationMs >= 3500 ? 'long' : 'short',
        position: entry.position,
      });
      // After Toast.show, find the last <pwa-toast> element
      const elements = document.querySelectorAll('pwa-toast');
      const el = elements[elements.length - 1] as HTMLElement | undefined;
      if (el) {
        (el as any).text = entry.text;
        el.setAttribute('data-position', entry.position);
      }
      // Wait for the duration
      await new Promise<void>((res) => setTimeout(res, entry.durationMs));
      // Remove the element before starting next
      if (el && el.parentNode) {
        el.parentNode.removeChild(el);
      }
      entry.resolve();
    } catch (err) {
      entry.reject(err);
    }
  }
}

const manager = new ToastQueueManager();

window.enqueueToast = (options: ToastOptions) => manager.enqueue(options);
window.drainToastQueue = () => manager.drain();
window.getQueueState = () => manager.getState();
```

Wait, there's a subtle issue. When `scheduleNext` is called from `enqueue` and the queue has items but is not active, the first `enqueue` call should immediately trigger display. But what if multiple synchronous `enqueue` calls happen — only the first one should activate, and the others should just be added to the queue.

Looking at my code: 
- enqueue A: pushes A to queue, calls scheduleNext, active is false, queue has 1 → shifts A, sets active=true, displays A
- enqueue B (sync, immediately after A): pushes B to queue, calls scheduleNext, active is now true → returns. 
- enqueue C (sync, immediately after B): same as B, pushed to queue, scheduleNext returns.
- After A finishes: active=false, queue has 2, calls scheduleNext → shifts B, displays B.

Looks good.

But wait, there's another concern. When the queue finishes processing A, I check `if (this.queue.length === 0)` to decide whether to notify idle resolvers. If queue is non-empty, I call `scheduleNext()` again. Good.

But there's a race condition where `scheduleNext` is called multiple times when active becomes false. Let me trace:
- After A done, `finally` runs: active=false, then since queue has items, scheduleNext() → shifts B, sets active=true, displays B.
- All synchronous calls within the `.finally()` callback. 

Now about the `displayToast` method. The Toast.show returns a Promise, and during that, the web plugin appends the `<pwa-toast>` element. So I should be able to find it after awaiting Toast.show.

But what if the queue of `pwa-toast` elements isn't pruned fast enough? Well, we manually remove each one before the next Toast.show, so there should only ever be one.

export interface EnqueueToastOptions {
  text: string;
  duration?: number | 'short' | 'long';
  position?: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom';
}

interface QueueEntry {
  text: string;
  durationMs: number;
  position: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom';
  resolve: () => void;
  reject: (err: unknown) => void;
}

export interface QueueState {
  pending: number;
  active: boolean;
}

/**
 * ToastQueueManager serializes Capacitor `Toast.show(...)` calls on the web so
 * that at most one `` element is ever visible at a time. Each
 * enqueued toast is shown for its configured duration and then removed from
 * the DOM before the next toast starts.
 */
export class ToastQueueManager {
  private readonly queue: QueueEntry[] = [];
  private active = false;
  private readonly idleResolvers: Array<() => void> = [];

  /** Enqueue a toast. Resolves once this toast has been displayed for its full
   *  duration AND its `` element has been removed from the DOM. */
  enqueue(options: EnqueueToastOptions): Promise {
    const text = String(options?.text ?? '');
    const position: 'top' | 'center' | 'bottom' =
      options?.position === 'top' || options?.position === 'center'
        ? options.position
        : 'bottom';
    const durationMs = this.resolveDuration(options?.duration);

    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const entry: QueueEntry = { text, durationMs, position, resolve, reject };
      this.queue.push(entry);
      // Kick the processor in case we are idle. Safe to call repeatedly; it
      // is a no-op while another toast is being displayed.
      this.scheduleNext();
    });
  }

  /** Returns a promise that resolves once the queue is empty AND no toast is
   *  currently being displayed. Resolves immediately when already idle. */
  drain(): Promise {
    if (this.queue.length === 0 && !this.active) {
      return Promise.resolve();
    }
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      this.idleResolvers.push(resolve);
    });
  }

  /** Synchronous snapshot of the queue. */
  getState(): QueueState {
    return { pending: this.queue.length, active: this.active };
  }

  private resolveDuration(d: EnqueueToastOptions['duration']): number {
    if (typeof d === 'number' && Number.isFinite(d) && d >= 0) {
      return d;
    }
    if (d === 'long') return 3500;
    // 'short' or undefined
    return 2000;
  }

  private scheduleNext(): void {
    if (this.active) return;
    if (this.queue.length === 0) {
      this.flushIdleResolvers();
      return;
    }
    const entry = this.queue.shift() as QueueEntry;
    this.active = true;
    // We deliberately do not await this here so scheduleNext returns
    // synchronously. The continuation handles the active flag.
    this.displayToast(entry).finally(() => {
      this.active = false;
      if (this.queue.length === 0) {
        this.flushIdleResolvers();
      } else {
        this.scheduleNext();
      }
    });
  }

  private flushIdleResolvers(): void {
    if (this.idleResolvers.length === 0) return;
    const resolvers = this.idleResolvers.splice(0, this.idleResolvers.length);
    for (const r of resolvers) r();
  }

  private async displayToast(entry: QueueEntry): Promise {
    try {
      // Use the real Toast.show — this appends a  element to
      // document.body. The web implementation resolves immediately after
      // appending; we own the actual display timing.
      await Toast.show({
        text: entry.text,
        duration: entry.durationMs >= 3500 ? 'long' : 'short',
        position: entry.position,
      });

      // After the plugin has appended the element, locate it. Because the
      // queue guarantees at most one  at a time, the (only)
      // current element is the one we just appended.
      const element = this.findCurrentToastElement();
      if (element) {
        // The plugin sets `message`; the spec also wants `text` available.
        (element as unknown as { text?: string }).text = entry.text;
        element.setAttribute('data-position', entry.position);
      }

      // Hold the toast visible for the configured duration.
      await delay(entry.durationMs);

      // Remove the element BEFORE starting the next toast so that no two
      //  elements ever coexist.
      if (element && element.parentNode) {
        element.parentNode.removeChild(element);
      }

      entry.resolve();
    } catch (err) {
      // Best-effort cleanup if something failed mid-flight.
      const element = this.findCurrentToastElement();
      if (element && element.parentNode) {
        try {
          element.parentNode.removeChild(element);
        } catch {
          /* ignore */
        }
      }
      entry.reject(err);
    }
  }

  private findCurrentToastElement(): HTMLElement | null {
    // There must be at most one  in the DOM at any time; pick it.
    return document.querySelector('pwa-toast');
  }
}

function delay(ms: number): Promise {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
}

// Bootstrap: create a single manager and expose it on `window`.
const manager = new ToastQueueManager();

declare global {
  interface Window {
    enqueueToast: (options: EnqueueToastOptions) => Promise;
    drainToastQueue: () => Promise;
    getQueueState: () => QueueState;
  }
}

window.enqueueToast = (options) => manager.enqueue(options);
window.drainToastQueue = () => manager.drain();
window.getQueueState = () => manager.getState();

function log(...parts: unknown[]): void {

  const line = parts

    .join(' ');
  logEl.textContent = `${new Date().toISOString()} ${line}\n${logEl.textContent ?? ''}`;
}
